newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Bank Melbourne sees 96/7 profit rise.
newsitem.headline: Bank Melbourne sees 96/7 profit rise.

text.p: Bank of Melbourne Ltd said on Tuesday that it expected to achieve higher earnings in 1996/97 (July-June).
The regional bank also said at a news conference that while profits would be higher, the level of growth would be less than that achieved in 1995/96.
"I'd be disappointed if we don't (grow profits)," chairman Christopher Stewart told reporters.
The bank earlier announced a net profit for the six months to December 13, 1996 of A$40.1 million against A$40.02 million previously.
It also said the outlook was positive for the second half.
"I'm actually reasonably confident that the second half will be quite good," Stewart said.
Stewart said a further cut in official interest rates by the Reserve Bank of Australia would push the bank's fees higher.
"If there's another interest rate cut then we'll adjust the fee structure," he said.
He added the regional bank's fees would remain lower relative to other regional and major players.

Stewart said while Bank of Melbourne's mortgage rates were usually adjusted soon after an official rate cut, the bank's predominantly retail-based source of funds meant there was a delay in commensurate reductions in deposit rates.
Acting chief executive officer Robert Giles said the bank's costs would increase in the second half but its cost to income ratio, a key performance measure, would improve.
"Costs are going to increase because we have added Challenge Bank staff and some infrastructure...Cost to income should improve," he said.
Giles said that the bank's was not planning to securitise its loan portfolio in fiscal 1996/97 although it could be securitised easily.
He said it would take a large increase in volumes of basic home loan products to tempt the bank to securitise its portfolio.
